packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-13 - unverified image-only reading

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE STATEMENT
- Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this fragment. This is a blind reading.
- Beyond the stated rules: I listed the packet directory to learn image filenames (packet.json not opened). I rotated image-006 and image-007 by 180 degrees (the text there is upside down) and cropped them in my scratchpad to read them. No web, search, edition or catalogue consulted.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- image-001 (overview): inside of a front wooden board of a bound volume. A parchment manuscript fragment is pasted on the board as a spine-lining / pastedown strip, partly covered at top and bottom by turned-in brown leather. A modern shelfmark label and a purple library stamp are on the board; on the right edge the first leaf of the host book is visible with red initials "O" (host book text, NOT part of the fragment; not read).
- image-002 (upper part) and image-003 (lower part) are native views of the fragment on the front board; they overlap by about 5 lines (image-003 ll.1-5 = image-002 ll.7-11).
- image-004: torn remnants of another pasted layer at the upper left of the front board (scraps with a few large letters).
- image-005 (overview): inside of the back board; a fragment strip is pasted with its text UPSIDE DOWN, between leather turn-ins. image-006 and image-007 are native views; when rotated 180 degrees, image-007 carries the upper text lines and image-006 the lower ones (they overlap by c. 4 lines).
- Script: gothic cursive / documentary-academic book hand, brown-black ink, very heavy abbreviation (scholastic style, with "d(icitu)r", "s(ecundu)m", "p(ro)b(ati)o", "i. d." etc.). Some words are underlined in brown-red ink (e.g. "ampliacio", "Appellacio", "sol(utio) aut(em) p(ate)t") which look like lemmata or section keywords. Ruled lines are visible on the back-board fragment. Interlinear additions occur (e.g. "hoc" written above a word in image-003 l.8). On the back fragment two lines are struck through with a horizontal stroke (deletions). A large "ll"/"lp" mark and marginal notes sit at the right side of the back fragment (upright orientation, left in the image) - possibly a marginal note or paragraph marker.
- Single column visible on each fragment; line beginnings at the left and ends at the right appear largely intact on the front fragment (right edge near the column edge), but the top and bottom lines are covered by leather.
- Tentative interpretation (not observation): a scholastic logic text (commentary with lemmata), with recurring terms "ampliacio", "appellacio", "distinctio", "suppositio", "sophisma", "probatio/improbatio", "solutio". Interpretation only.

LIMITATIONS
- Top and bottom lines of both fragments are covered by leather turn-ins. Some words in the left half of the front fragment are abraded (ink lost where paste/lining lifted). The back fragment is upside down and partly creased. Heavy abbreviation means many expansions are tentative.
- Line numbers count from the top of each tile AS PHOTOGRAPHED for image-002/003. For image-006/007 I give line numbers counted from the top of the image AFTER 180-degree rotation (stated per line), since the text is unreadable as photographed.

SPANS SELECTED
1. Front fragment, image-002 ll.1-11 and image-003 ll.6-19 (whole visible column).
2. Back fragment, rotated image-007 and rotated image-006 (whole visible column).
3. image-004 scraps (few letters only).

TRANSCRIPTION

== Front-board fragment (overview image-001) ==
image-002 l.1   ...[covered by leather] p(?)i ... ...
image-002 l.2   distinctione(m)[?] des...ctione(m)[?] q(uod) z opp(osi)to[?] a(m)pli(a)-
image-002 l.3   tio(n)i. ... [abraded] ...lari[?] d(icitu)r[?] ...dato. quid sit[?]
image-002 l.4   Ampliacio ... [abraded] ...q(uo)d[?] int(elligitu)r[?] ... p(?)o(st)[?] mag(is)
image-002 l.5   elucidat(ur)[?] ... ...ponit[?] distin(ctionem)[?] ip(s)i(us)
image-002 l.6   ampliacio(n)is ibi. Ampliacio e(st) sic z      ("Ampliacio" underlined)
image-002 l.7   ...p(?)l(?) d(icitu)r m. d. ... s(ecundu)m n. ampliacio(n)is
image-002 l.8   pote(st)[?] ...ndi[?] [abraded] ...tet clat[?] ei(us) m(od)o[?]
image-002 l.9   ...cedo[?] pote(st) [abraded] ...m ibi. z io se(cundu)m[?] d(icitu)r. que      ("z io se(cundu)m" underlined)
image-002 l.10  ... d(icitu)r i. d. s(ecundu)m n. ...pd[?] soph(isma)[?] z argum(en)to      (left edge partly obscured by label)

== Torn scraps at upper left of front board (image-004) ==

== Back-board fragment (overview image-005); text upside down. Line numbers counted after rotating each image 180 degrees ==

image-007 (rotated) l.8   p(ro)ced(it)[?] q(uod). si ... d(icitu)r ... m(od)o. p(ro)p(ter) i-      ("p(ro)ced(it)" underlined)

image-006 (rotated) ll.1-3 repeat image-007 (rotated) ll.7-9.
image-006 (rotated) l.4   potest dist(inctio)nem[?]. q(uod) d(icitu)r v.      ("q(uod) d(icitu)r v." underlined; interlinear "en"[?] above d(icitu)r)
image-006 (rotated) l.5   Ind(e) p(ate)t est dist(inctio) z ea(m) exp(lanat)-
image-006 (rotated) l.6   ib(i). z q(uod) ad hoc q(uod)[?] i(n) q(uo)...      ("z q(uod) ad hoc" underlined)
image-006 (rotated) l.7   q(uod)[?] ex distinctione p(ro)cedit[?] o(mn)ia m-      (marginal "ll"/"lp" sign to the right in the margin)
image-006 (rotated) l.8   a(m)pl(i)atu(m)[?] ... ibi. Sol(utio)[?] aut(em) p(ate)t      ("Sol(utio) aut(em) p(ate)t" underlined; marginal note at far right "...p(ro)[?] d(icitu)r[?]")
image-006 (rotated) l.9   In v(?). et q(ui)[?] ... soph(isma)[?] ...p(ro)p(ositi)onem[?]
image-006 (rotated) l.10  ...b(?)t ...i(n)[?] ...ta[?] soluit d(icitu)r[?]
image-006 (rotated) l.11  ...edi s(ed)[?] illa p(ro)p(ositi)o ibi      (lighter brown ink)
image-006 (rotated) l.12  ...[covered by leather]

MOST SECURE READINGS FOR A LATER MATCH
Front: "ampliacio(n)is ibi. Ampliacio e(st) sic" (002 l.6); "Secu(n)da p(ar)s" (003 l.6); "de a(m)pliacione" (003 l.9); "Appellacio ... ibi. appella-/tio(n)i" (003 ll.10-11); "appellacio(n)is z ea(m) explanat" (003 l.12); "ad supp(ositi)o(n)em" (003 l.13); "soph(isma) z argum(en)to" (002 l.10).
Back: "acceptione(s)" (007r l.5); "declinacione(m)" (007r l.6); "Ind(e) p(ate)t est dist(inctio) z ea(m) exp-" (006r l.5); "ex distinctione p(ro)cedit" (006r l.7); "Sol(utio) aut(em) p(ate)t" (006r l.8); "illa p(ro)p(ositi)o ibi" (006r l.11).

SUGGESTIONS
Lifting or imaging under the leather turn-ins would recover the covered top and bottom lines; raking light could help with the abraded left half of the front fragment.
